doc.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Motohiko Hino's date and New Year's gigs in Japan
summary: They remember drummer Toko Hino, Joe Henderson in Japan, and Liebman's New Year's concerts with Japanese musicians who played bridge all night.

blocks.x: Here’s a date for Motohiko Hino, a great drummer who’s no longer with us.
Toko’s date that we did up at Swallow’s – in what’s her name? Carla Bley’s thing up there. I think we did . . .
Yep. That’s what we did up there. That was Toko’s date.
It was something. He got sick, something. He was a great cat. What a great drummer.
The first time I ever heard him is on Joe Henderson in Japan . . .
. . . which is like an announcement for Americans that you could have a hip Japanese rhythm section.

Thank you. Exactly, and the piano player was good. I used to spend – I did a couple of New Years – New Year’s a big deal in Japan. Takes a week off and everybody – you do concerts at 3 o’clock in the afternoon. I was invited a couple times with those guys. I did it with Toko and a piano player, Fukiyama, whatever. I forget. He played with Elvin eventually. Karashima. Something like that. We had a great time. Then they would play bridge all night. I would just sit there with a bottle of Scotch and watch them play bridge. They weren’t even playing for money. They just played. It was like a New Year’s custom or something.
